{"consolidated_memory":"## Latency Spikes in ml/serving/batcher.py - Three Separate Incidents

All three incidents involved the same component (ml/serving/batcher.py, ml pipeline side) and shared a common diagnostic signal: a tail far above the median in the serving histogram. All were reproduced using the mixed-size request trace. However, they had distinct triggers, root causes, and fixes.

### Incident 1: Cold-Start Latency Spike [2026-03-10]
**Trigger:** Latency spike appeared only on the first request after a cold start.
**Root Cause:** Off-by-one in the slice bound.
**Result:** Flaky test went from 4 failures per hundred runs to zero.
**Fix:** Corrected the bound and added a property test around it.
**PR:** #3155 on branch fix/latency-spike-1

### Incident 2: Post-Retry Latency Spike [2026-03-30]
**Trigger:** Latency spike appeared only after the client had already retried once.
**Root Cause:** Error swallowed by a bare except clause.
**Result:** Job finished in 89 minutes instead of 9 hours (6x improvement).
**Fix:** Narrowed the exception handler and let the failure propagate.
**PR:** #3169 on branch fix/latency-spike-2

### Incident 3: Race Condition Latency Spike [2026-08-20]
**Trigger:** Latency spike appeared when two requests raced on the same key.
**Root Cause:** Two writes that were never wrapped in a transaction.
**Result:** Throughput rose 75 percent, to 115 requests per second.
**Fix:** Wrapped both writes in one transaction.
**PR:** #8159 on branch fix/latency-spike-3

**Context:** All three incidents involved the same corner of ml/serving/batcher.py, allowing context to carry over across the fixes."}
